note: A LaTeX paper of 23 pages with five printed tables and no figures at all - the first paper in this lane whose figure list is empty. All five grids are boxed the same way (top rule, doubled header rule, a rule between every body row, closing rule, verticals at every cell boundary), none is shaded, and all five captions print below their grid, the inverse of the sibling paper three rows up the queue. Four of the five tables are one two-column Metric/Value template repeated for the two current and two proposed plans, each with eleven data rows and an italic, ruled-off L row; only Table 5 differs, with a two-tier header over five columns and the paper's only decimal-aligned figures. Four of the five print a page after their announcing sentence. Two grids lose a value in the text layer (P7 on p14, P5 on p17) and both print cleanly in the raster - the only misalignment this paper has is an extraction artefact.
rules: This paper prints no figures at all: all five measured regions are tables, so the figure list is empty and every geometry field the schema defines is unused here [table.rows].
All five captions print below their grid, the inverse of the sibling paper three rows up this queue where every table caption printed above; the side is per paper, never per table [caption.position].
Every caption is numbered with a colon - 'Table 1:' through 'Table 5:' - and no other numbering form appears anywhere in the paper [caption.numbering].
All five grids are boxed the same way: top rule, a doubled rule under the header, a rule between every body row, a closing rule at the foot, and verticals at every cell boundary [table.rule_style].
No grid is shaded; there is no zebra striping and no coloured cell anywhere in the paper [table.zebra].

Four of the five tables are one template four times - a two-column Metric/Value grid with eleven data rows whose last row, L, is ruled off and italicised - so only Table 5 differs in shape [table.rows].
Only Table 5 carries two header rows, because it needs a city band over an L/ΔL line; the four metric grids carry a single 'Metric | Value' header [table.header_rows].
Only Table 5 merges cells, spanning each city name over its two value columns; the four metric grids have no spanning cell [table.merged_cells].
Only Table 5 aligns its figures on a decimal point - the four metric grids centre their values, so 0.05 and 0.5535 do not share a point column [table.decimal_aligned].
Widths are decided by the number of columns, not by importance: the four metric grids are a narrow centred block of about 0.14 of the page while Table 5 takes about half the text width [table.width].

Four of the five tables print a page after the sentence that announces them (pp8, 10 and 17 for pp9, 11 and 18), and the two that print on their own page are the two proposed-plan grids [mention.lead_pages].
Each table is named exactly once in the running text and the citation always carries the number - this paper has no uncited exhibit and no exhibit cited by deixis alone [mention.count].
Two citation grammars: 'Table N summarizes ...' with the table as subject, and '... are summarized in Table N' with the table as a prepositional object [mention.lead_pattern].
The house citation form is the capitalised 'Table N' with no colon (the colon belongs to the caption line only) [mention.style].

Captions run 19 to 20 words and are single sentences of the form 'Table of ... for <plan> of <city>'; none states a unit, a condition or a conclusion, and all are nominal phrases with no verb [caption.words].

Two of the four metric grids show a one-row shift in the text layer - p14 drops the P7 value and p17 drops the P5 value - and in both cases the raster prints every value on its label's row, so the shift is an extraction artefact and not a printed defect [table.numeric_cols].
The record carries no note sentences at all: not one of the five grids prints a note line under it, and the only prose about each table follows it in the running text [table.note_sentence].

Exhibit size never tracks exhibit importance here - the table that carries the paper's headline comparison (Table 5) is the largest, but the three plan grids that state the success levels the abstract quotes are the three smallest at 0.031 of the page each [place.area_frac].

Each grid belongs to one subsection and follows it: the two current-plan grids under the result kind of sections 3.1 and 3.2, the two proposed-plan grids under the solution kind of 4.1 and 4.2, and the initiative comparison back under result in 4.3 [place.section_kind].
No table continues across a page turn in this paper, even though four of the five floats move off their announcing page [table.continued].
